text:
maria: FYI - ran longctx kv-reuse suite (30k token streams) and saw steady memory growth / fragmentation that correlates with prefix reuse patterns. p50/95 token gen went up and evictions spiked. attaching quick summary link: https://internal/ops/kv-longctx-2187 :eyes:
perf-bot: alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate up 3.8x over baseline on longctx-tests at 2026-03-18T14:02Z
alex: Can you paste the snippet of the cache key format and the eviction logs?
kai: Short dump below. Note current key = `tenant:session_prefix:request_hash` where `request_hash = sha256(prefix+body)[0:16]`. We see many slightly different prefixes due to punctuation/whitespace => low reuse. Logs:
```
EVICT count=312 free_mem=1.2GB fragmentation=0.18 pages_swapped=42
ALLOC id=0x7f9a9b size=24576 key=tenant-a:Hello world:0x3f2a...
ALLOC id=0x7f9a9c size=49152 key=tenant-a:Hello world!:0x4b9d...
ALLOC id=0x7f9a9d size=65536 key=tenant-a:Hello, world:0x8f1e...
CACHE_HIT prefix_normalized=0.12 reuse=0.08
```
maria: Profiling numbers: baseline (no regression) p50=18ms p95=120ms mem_resident=2.1GB. Regression run: p50=24ms p95=260ms mem_resident=2.54GB (+440MB), steady climb over 10k tokens. Heap fragmentation correlates with many small allocs from slight prefix variants.
jamal: Sounds like cache key churn + fragmentation. Two angles: normalize prefix (trim/punct/lowercase) and change hashing to faster low-collide hash (xxhash64) + fixed-length fingerprint so allocations align. Also consider session stickiness TTL to avoid cross-request key churn.
alex: Agree. Small experiment proposal:
1) Normalize prefixes: `normalize_prefix(s)->truncate(64)`
2) Key = `tenant|prefix_fingerprint|session_salt` where `prefix_fingerprint = xxh64(normalized_prefix)`
3) Sticky TTL = 30s for ephemeral sessions, configurable per tenant
4) Add periodic compaction: when free_mem < threshold run compact_arena()
Config snippet to test: 
```
{"kv": {"prefix_norm": true, "prefix_max_len": 64, "fingerprint_algo": "xxh64", "sticky_ttl_s": 30, "compaction_threshold_mb": 256}}
```
kai: Quick bench (local dev rig, 8V100) with normalization + xxh64 + ttl=30s: p50=19ms p95=130ms mem_resident=2.18GB, eviction_rate ~baseline. Fragmentation metric down from 0.18 -> 0.06.
perf-bot: note: regression ticket created: PERF-2187, assigned to eng-runtime, priority=P2
maria: Nice. A few follow-ups:
- Need a backwards-compatible key migration strategy (older in-memory entries may still exist). Can we include `version_byte` in the key so compaction can coalesce old entries?
- We should run a canary with 5% traffic on dedicated pools and a synthetic longctx load for 24h.
jamal: For migration: include `kvv1|` vs `kvv2|` prefix on keys so the runtime can treat kvv1 entries as stale and evict them lazily. For compaction we can scan low-hit segments.
alex: I'll open a PR with implementation + unit tests (hash correctness, normalization cases, TTL behavior). Can we also add an e2e perf test that simulates punctuation-heavy prefixes to ensure reuse actually improves?
kai: I'll run the 24h canary on a dedicated pool and collect p50/p95, mem, evict_rate, fragmentation, page_faults. Will share a dashboard.
maria: Good plan. If canary looks good, rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72h with automated rollback on eviction_rate > 2x baseline or p95 > 2x baseline.
alex: tagging @kai for the canary runs and @jamal for compaction logic review. :thumbsup:
